classification.difficultyReason: Choose trial roots, use the Factor Theorem to reduce each cubic, factor the remaining quadratic, then translate multiplicities and leading signs into sketches.

content.prompt: Sketch the graphs of each of the following polynomials by first using the Factor Theorem:

answer.short: $y=(x+1)(x-1)(x-2)$. Crosses at $x=-1,1,2$; $y$-intercept $(0,2)$. Left end down, right end up.
answer.worked:
$P(-1)=-1-2+1+2=0$, so $x+1$ is a factor.

$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x+1)(x^2-3x+2)\\P(x)&=(x+1)(x-1)(x-2)\\P(0)&=(1)(-1)(-2)=2\end{align*}$$

All three roots are simple, so the graph crosses the $x$-axis at $-1,1,2$. The positive cubic leading term gives a downward left end and an upward right end.

answer.short: $y=(x+2)(x+1)(x-1)$. Crosses at $x=-2,-1,1$; $y$-intercept $(0,-2)$. Left end down, right end up.
answer.worked:
$P(1)=1+2-1-2=0$, so $x-1$ is a factor.

$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x-1)(x^2+3x+2)\\P(x)&=(x-1)(x+1)(x+2)\\P(0)&=(-1)(1)(2)=-2\end{align*}$$

All three roots are simple, so the graph crosses at $-2,-1,1$. The positive cubic leading term gives a downward left end and an upward right end.

answer.short: $y=-(x+2)(x+1)(x-3)$. Crosses at $x=-2,-1,3$; $y$-intercept $(0,6)$. Left end up, right end down.
answer.worked:
$P(-1)=1-7+6=0$, so $x+1$ is a factor.

$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x+1)(-x^2+x+6)\\P(x)&=-(x+1)(x+2)(x-3)\\P(0)&=-(1)(2)(-3)=6\end{align*}$$

All roots are simple, so the graph crosses at $-2,-1,3$. The negative cubic leading term gives an upward left end and a downward right end.

answer.short: $y=(x+4)(x+2)(x-3)$. Crosses at $x=-4,-2,3$; $y$-intercept $(0,-24)$. Left end down, right end up.
answer.worked:
$P(-2)=-8+12+20-24=0$, so $x+2$ is a factor.

$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x+2)(x^2+x-12)\\P(x)&=(x+2)(x+4)(x-3)\\P(0)&=(2)(4)(-3)=-24\end{align*}$$

All roots are simple, so the graph crosses at $-4,-2,3$. The positive cubic leading term gives a downward left end and an upward right end.

answer.short: $y=-(x-2)^2(x-4)$. Touches at $x=2$ and crosses at $x=4$; $y$-intercept $(0,16)$. Left end up, right end down.
answer.worked:
$P(2)=-8+32-40+16=0$, so $x-2$ is a factor.

$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x-2)(-x^2+6x-8)\\P(x)&=-(x-2)^2(x-4)\\P(0)&=-(-2)^2(-4)=16\end{align*}$$

The root $2$ has multiplicity $2$, so the graph touches the axis there from above. The simple root $4$ is a crossing. The negative cubic leading term gives an upward left end and a downward right end.

answer.short: $y=(x+3)(x+2)^2$. Crosses at $x=-3$ and touches at $x=-2$; $y$-intercept $(0,12)$. Left end down, right end up.
answer.worked:
$P(-2)=-8+28-32+12=0$, so $x+2$ is a factor.

$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x+2)(x^2+5x+6)\\P(x)&=(x+2)^2(x+3)\\P(0)&=(2)^2(3)=12\end{align*}$$

The simple root $-3$ is a crossing. The root $-2$ has multiplicity $2$, so the graph touches the axis there from above. The positive cubic leading term gives a downward left end and an upward right end.

answer.short: $y=-(x+3)^2(x-2)$. Touches at $x=-3$ and crosses at $x=2$; $y$-intercept $(0,18)$. Left end up, right end down.
answer.worked:
$P(-3)=27-36-9+18=0$, so $x+3$ is a factor.

$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x+3)(-x^2-x+6)\\P(x)&=-(x+3)^2(x-2)\\P(0)&=-(3)^2(-2)=18\end{align*}$$

The double root $-3$ is a touch from above; the simple root $2$ is a crossing. The negative cubic leading term gives an upward left end and a downward right end.

answer.worked:

$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x+2)(2x^2-7x+3)\\P(x)&=(x+2)(2x-1)(x-3)\\P(0)&=(2)(-1)(-3)=6\end{align*}$$

All roots are simple, so the graph crosses at $-2,\frac12,3$. The positive cubic leading term gives a downward left end and an upward right end.

answer.short: $y=(x-4)(2x+3)(3x-1)$. Crosses at $x=-\frac32,\frac13,4$; $y$-intercept $(0,12)$. Left end down, right end up.
answer.worked:
$P(4)=384-272-124+12=0$, so $x-4$ is a factor.

$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x-4)(6x^2+7x-3)\\P(x)&=(x-4)(2x+3)(3x-1)\\P(0)&=(-4)(3)(-1)=12\end{align*}$$

All roots are simple, so the graph crosses at $-\frac32,\frac13,4$. The positive cubic leading term gives a downward left end and an upward right end.

answer.short: $y=(2x-1)(2x+3)(3x+2)$. Crosses at $x=-\frac32,-\frac23,\frac12$; $y$-intercept $(0,-6)$. Left end down, right end up.
answer.worked:
$P(\frac12)=\frac32+5-\frac12-6=0$, so $2x-1$ is a factor.

$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(2x-1)(6x^2+13x+6)\\P(x)&=(2x-1)(2x+3)(3x+2)\\P(0)&=(-1)(3)(2)=-6\end{align*}$$

All roots are simple, so the graph crosses at $-\frac32,-\frac23,\frac12$. The positive cubic leading term gives a downward left end and an upward right end.
